hook: "🚨🚨🚨 7,500+ winning Meta ads, sorted by format, free."
body: A mega-directory of 7,500+ winning Meta ads pre-sorted into format boards: 2,700 top-50 DTC winners, 1,300 beauty, 650 printing ads, 540 native statics with long copy, 430 listicles, 350 shock-and-gross, 330 BOFU offer, 270 advertorial/presell, 240 AI/CGI, 230 founder video, 230 ad+lander pairs, 220 statics that beat video.
cta: "Save this one" — bookmark the thread; links to each gethookd board.
idea: Pre-sorted format boards replace creative briefs: hand your team 7,500 winners organized by format instead of a blank brief.
sequencing: Value jab: agencies charge retainers for a tenth of this.
The 12 boards, each with a count (2,700 DTC … 220 statics-that-beat-video).
Directive: hand this to your creative team instead of a brief.
formatting: Long directory post with 12 board links and counts; no ad creative itself. Curator authority voice.
why_it_works: Staggering specificity (exact counts per board) makes the free resource feel like a paid product, and "save this" converts the value into a bookmark metric.
what_to_steal: The insight LC can operationalize immediately: sort its own swipe by format and hand teams pre-sorted boards instead of blank briefs — plus the "shock & gross" bucket as a reminder that the gross-out slot exists even in jewelry (tarnish, green-skin close-ups).

body: A competitive-intel breakdown of 4 dog-joint-pain advertisers all running 200+ days: Helio Pet's "SCAM ALERT ⭐ turns out it actually works?" static → advertorial (334d); Tailwindpets' 63-media hinged-brace DCO carousel → product page (603d); Cannanine's dog + handwritten "Nature's Painkillers!" sticky-note UGC → story page (244d); Zoomies' "My Dog's Joint Pain is GONE!!" quote carousel → advertorial (202d); plus Posh Dog's 3-panel condition static (276d). Closes with a copy-paste MCP prompt to map any symptom the same way.
cta: Copy-paste GetHookd MCP prompt ("Prompt maps ANY symptom") — engagement CTA, no product sold.
idea: Days-active is the truth serum: four brands prove multiple formats can print on one symptom for 200-600 days; the deliverable is a reusable prompt to repeat the mapping on any niche.
sequencing: Hook: one symptom, 4 formats, all 200+ days.
The table: brand | format | lander | offer | days active (Helio 334d, Tailwind 603d, Cannanine 244d, Zoomies 202d, Posh 276d).
Tool: paste-in MCP prompt to map any symptom (search → group by format/lander → concept per format → offer benchmark).
formatting: Data-dense text post: brand · format · lander · offer · days-active table + a full MCP prompt. One photo of a dog ad.
why_it_works: Longevity numbers (603 days!) do the arguing — no persuasion needed when the scoreboard shows a carousel outliving most brands.
what_to_steal: The days-active table as LC's own reporting format (format | lander | offer | days) and the multi-format-on-one-symptom lesson: LC can run the same pain point (tarnish/green skin) across static, carousel, UGC, and quote formats simultaneously.

hook: "Gross ads get banned in every 'clean creative' guide. They keep making money anyway."
body: The thesis: gross visuals (the parasite, the plaque, the gunk in your pillow) earn a 2-second thumb-stop, and the ad spends those 2 seconds explaining the MECHANISM — not showing the product. Includes a 36s video demo.
cta: none visible (link to the demo video).
idea: The gross image buys 2 seconds of attention; the mechanism explanation — not the product shot — is what converts.
sequencing: Contrarian hook: banned by guides, still printing.
Rule: use the 2s to explain HOW it works, not to show the product.
formatting: Short thesis post + 36s video. Minimal, punchy, contrarian.
why_it_works: Disgust is a hardwired attention hijack, and pairing it with mechanism-education converts revulsion into curiosity instead of a scroll-past.
what_to_steal: The sequencing rule for LC's "problem" creatives: open on the ugly close-up (tarnished chain, green-skin wrist, irritated neck) and spend the first 2 seconds explaining the waterproof PVD mechanism — never lead with the pretty product shot.
